## Root cause of the timeout mode, reproduced deterministically; fix in progress (2026-11-16)

**Reproduction (Trace2 preserved, `--basetemp` under the worktree).** Scaling the store's per-call git bound (`event_commit_git._GIT_TIMEOUT`) from 120 s to 1 s in a copy of the origin/main test reproduces the observed failure on every run: 3 of 3 raised `rebar create failed (exit 1): Error: git commit failed while holding lock: git timed out after 1.0s` inside `_create_two_tickets_traced`. The preserved trace of an unscaled run shows the mechanism: the first ticket-create's `git commit` (3.7 s total, idle host) spends 3.6 s in its child `git maintenance run --auto --no-detach` -> `git repack -d -l -q --cruft` -> `pack-objects` over the 20,000 loose objects the fixture wrote. The detector's fill makes the commit it watches carry an O(fill) repack under a wall-clock bound, so its duration scales with host load.

**This is a 4th mechanism, not one of the three candidates** in the description: git did start maintenance inside the commit (the thing the detector looks for), but the repack did not finish within the bound, so the create raised before the detector could assert. It accounts for 5 of the 6 recorded failures (2026-10-31, 11-01, 11-02 x2, plus the 11-02 isolated rerun).

**Why it stopped failing without a fix.** af8f67df7b3 (2026-11-03, `Give store event writes the local git bound`) raised `_GIT_TIMEOUT` from 30 s to `_LOCAL_GIT_TIMEOUT` = 120 s. Every recorded timeout predates it. On current origin/main (b4e0d01b649) I ran the unmodified detector 24 times in 6 parallel lanes beside 14 CPU busy-loops (load average 26 -> 52 on 18 CPUs): 24 of 24 passed, but the slowest commit per run took 19.2-28.8 s. So the old shape still spends up to ~29 s per run inside the bounded commit and passes only on the 4x margin of the raised bound; the class is not fixed, just further from the edge.

**Fix (tests/unit/test_store_commit_maintenance_bd66.py only, no production change).** The detector now crosses a minimal threshold instead of the 20,000-object fill: it writes 2 loose objects whose ids start with `17` (the directory git's gc strategy samples) and sets `gc.auto=1` and `maintenance.geometric-repack.auto=1` at command scope (GIT_CONFIG_COUNT env, which outranks the store's config). `gc.auto=1` alone did NOT trigger anything on this host's git 2.56, whose default auto-maintenance strategy is geometric; the second key covers it. Result: the commit's repack runs over ~30 objects, in ~0.1 s total. With the 1 s scaled bound the fixed detector passes 3 of 3. With the suppression KEPT, the fixed detector still fails and its diagnosis says `git started no auto-maintenance under any process: it chose not to run it`, so it remains able to fail. The repack-survival sibling test keeps the 20,000-object fill (it needs it, and its commits carry the suppression) and now also asserts the gc strategy's sampled threshold (`objects/17` > 27).

**The 2026-10-26 assertion mode stays unreproduced.** It is the only occurrence (`commits >= 1`, no maintenance descendant). By git's `prepare_auto_maintenance`, a successful commit spawns `maintenance run --auto` unless `maintenance.auto=false` is in effect, so that signature means the traced commit ran with suppression. One code path does that despite the test's patches: `event_append._recover_from_unmerged` / `_recover_from_invalid_object` retry the commit with their own imported `_AUTOMAINT_OFF`, which the test does not patch. Whether a recovery fired on 10-26 is unknown (the trace is gone). The fix keeps Gerrit 3135's diagnosis on that path. If it recurs, the message will name it.
